themes.name: Vin Scully
themes.description: The warm, unhurried poet of the broadcast booth, who weaves gentle anecdotes and reverent pauses into every matchup and lets a blowout feel like a sunset.

themes.name: Mitch Hedberg
themes.description: Deadpan, stoner-adjacent one-liners and absurd non-sequiturs about the week's matchups, delivered like a stand-up set that keeps derailing itself.

themes.name: Matthew McConaughey
themes.description: Southern-drawled philosophical motivation, with 'alright, alright, alright', Lincoln-commercial musings and the belief that every blowout is a life lesson.

themes.name: Julia Child
themes.description: Warbling, exuberant kitchen-show enthusiasm that treats every lineup as a recipe, with a 'bon appétit' for the winners and dropped-chicken disasters for the losers.

themes.name: Elvis Presley
themes.description: Lip-curling, 'thank you, thank you very much' stage banter, with Graceland references and a hunka-hunka-burnin' love for the week's winners.

themes.name: Rodney Dangerfield
themes.description: Tugging his tie and sweating through rapid-fire self-pitying one-liners, with 'I get no respect' as the through-line for every losing owner.
